'''Alice Guionnet''' (born 24 May 1969)<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb130886015.public|title = Guionnet}}</ref> is a French [[mathematician]] known for her work in [[probability theory]], in particular on large [[random matrix|random matrices]].

== Biography ==
Guionnet entered the [[École Normale Supérieure]] (Paris) in 1989.
She earned her PhD in 1995 under the supervision of [[Gérard Ben Arous]] at [[University of Paris-Sud]]. Focuses of her academic research can be viewed in her thesis, ''Dynamique de Langevin d'un verre de spins'' ([[Langevin dynamics|Langevin Dynamics]] of spin glass).

She has held positions at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences|Courant Institute]], 
[[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]], [[MIT]], and [[École Normale Supérieure|ENS (Paris)]]. She is currently a
Director of Research at [[École normale supérieure de Lyon|ENS de Lyon]].<ref>[http://perso.ens-lyon.fr/aguionne/cvanglais17.pdf Curriculum Vitae]</ref>

== Works ==
Alice Guionnet is known for her work on large random matrices.<ref>{{cite book|language=english|author1=G. Anderson|author2=A. Guionnet|author3=O. Zeitouni|name-list-style=amp|title=An introduction to random matrices|series=Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics, 118|editor=Cambridge University Press|date=2010|isbn=9780511801334}}</ref> In this context, she established principles of large deviations for the empirical measurements of the eigenvalues of large random matrices with [[Gérard Ben Arous]]<ref>{{cite journal|language=english|author1=G. Ben Arous|author2=A. Guionnet|name-list-style=amp|title=Large deviations for Wigner's law and Voiculescu's non-commutative entropy|journal=Probab. Theory Relat.|date=1997|volume=108|issue=4|pages=517–542|doi=10.1007/s004400050119|s2cid=17415771}}</ref> and [[Ofer Zeitouni]],<ref>{{cite journal|language=english|author1=A. Guionnet|author2=O. Zeitouni|name-list-style=amp|title=Large deviations asymptotics for spherical integrals|journal=Journal of Functional Analysis|date=2002|volume=188|issue=2|pages=461–515|doi=10.1006/jfan.2001.3833|doi-access=free}}</ref> applied the theory of concentration of measure, initiated the rigorous study of matrices with a heavy tail, and obtained the convergence of spectral measurement of non-normal matrices.<ref>{{cite journal|language=english|author1=A. Guionnet|author2=M. Krishnapur|author3=et O. Zeitouni|title=The single ring theorem|journal=Annals of Mathematics|date=2011|volume=174|issue=2|pages=1189–1217|doi=10.4007/annals.2011.174.2.10|doi-access=free}}</ref> She developed the analysis of Dyson-Schwinger equations to obtain topological asymptotic expansions,<ref>{{cite journal|language=english|author1=A. Guionnet|author2=E. Maurel Segala|name-list-style=amp|title=Combinatorial aspects of matrix models|journal=Alea|date=2006|volume=1|pages=241–279|bibcode=2005math......3064G|arxiv=math/0503064}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|language=english|author1=B. Collins|author2=A. Guionnet|author3=E. Maurel Segala|name-list-style=amp|title=Asymptotics of unitary and orthogonal matrix integrals|journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|date=2009|volume=222|pages=172–215|doi=10.1016/j.aim.2009.03.019|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0608193|s2cid=18359348}}</ref> and studied changes in beta-models<ref>{{cite journal|language=english|author1=G. Borot|author2=A. Guionnet|name-list-style=amp|title=Asymptotic expansion of beta matrix models in the one-cut regime|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|date=2013|volume=317|issue=2|pages=447–483|doi=10.1007/s00220-012-1619-4|arxiv=1107.1167|bibcode=2013CMaPh.317..447B|s2cid=17256336}}</ref> and random tilings.<ref>{{cite journal|language=english|author1=A. Borodin|author2=V. Gorin|author3=A. Guionnet|name-list-style=amp|title=Gaussian asymptotics of discrete $\beta$-ensembles|journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS|date=2017|volume=125|pages=1–78|doi=10.1007/s10240-016-0085-5|arxiv=1505.03760|s2cid=119575140}}</ref> In collaboration with [[Alessio Figalli]],<ref>{{cite journal|language=english|author1=F. Bekerman|author2=A. Figalli|author3=et A. Guionnet|title=Transport maps for Beta-matrix models and Universality|journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics|date=2015|volume=338|issue=2|pages=589–619|doi=10.1007/s00220-015-2384-y|arxiv=1311.2315|bibcode=2015CMaPh.338..589B |s2cid=119031960}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|language=english|author1=A.Figalli|author2=A. Guionnet|name-list-style=amp|title=Universality in several-matrix models via approximate transport maps|journal=Acta Mathematica|date=2016|volume=217|pages=81–176|doi=10.1007/s11511-016-0142-4|arxiv=1407.2759|s2cid=119321046}}</ref> she introduced the concept of approximate transport to demonstrate the universality of local fluctuations.

Alice Guionnet also demonstrated significant results in free probabilities by comparing Voiculescu entropies,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=P. Biane|author2=M. Capitaine|author3=A. Guionnet|name-list-style=amp|title=Large deviation bounds for matrix Brownian motion|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|date=2003|volume=152|issue=2|pages=433–459|doi=10.1007/s00222-002-0281-4|bibcode=2003InMat.152..433B|s2cid=120016671}}</ref> building with [[Vaughan Jones]] and [[Dimitri Shlyakhtenko]] a round of subfactors from planar algebras of any index,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=A. Guionnet|author2=V. Jones|author3=D. Shlyakhtenko|name-list-style=amp|title=Random matrices, free probability, planar algebras and subfactors|journal=Quantas of Math|date=2010|pages=201–239}}</ref> and establishing isomorphisms between the algebras of von Neumann generated by q-Gaussian variables by constructing free transport.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=A. Guionnet|author2=V. Jones|author3=D. Shlyakhtenko|name-list-style=amp|title=Free monotone transport|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|date=2014|volume=197|issue=3|pages=613–661|doi=10.1007/s00222-013-0493-9|bibcode=2014InMat.197..613G|arxiv=1204.2182|s2cid=16882208}}</ref>

== Distinctions ==
The [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach]] awarded her the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach#Oberwolfach Prize|Oberwolfach Prize]] in 1998.

In 2003 she was awarded the [[Rollo Davidson Prize#List of recipients of the Rollo Davidson Prize|Rollo Davidson Prize]] for her work in probability.<ref>{{cite book|language=english|author1=James M. Hill|author2=Ross Moore|name-list-style=amp |title=Applied Mathematics Entering the 21st Century: Invited Talks from the ICIAM 2003 Congress |editor=SIAM |editor-link=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |year=2004 |volume= 116 |page=162 |isbn=978-0898715590 }}</ref>

In 2006, the [[French Academy of Sciences]] awarded her the [[Prix Paul Doistau–Émile Blutet]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/activite/prix/laureat_06.pdf |title= Paul Doistau-Émile Blutet Prize (Mathématique)|author=Académie des sciences|author-link= Académie des sciences (France) |access-date=2019-01-26}}</ref>

For her contributions, she won the 2009 [[Loève Prize]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200910/rtx091001302p.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|title=Guionnet Awarded 2009 Loève Prize|department=Mathematics People|page=1302|volume=56|issue=10|date=November 2009}}</ref>

In 2012 she became a [[Simons Investigator]].<ref>[https://www.simonsfoundation.org/mathematics-physical-sciences/simons-investigators/simons-investigators-awardees/ Simons Investigators Awardees], The Simons Foundation</ref> She was elected to the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 2017.{{r|esa}} She is also a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://imstat.org/honored-ims-fellows/|title=Honored IMS Fellows|access-date=2020-07-01}}</ref>

Guinnet is the 2018 winner of the Blaise Pascal Medal in Mathematics of the European Academy of Sciences.<ref name=esa>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurasc.org/medals/pb_medals_18.asp|title=The Blaise Pascal Medals 2018|publisher=European Academy of Sciences|access-date=2019-02-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190120144500/http://www.eurasc.org/medals/pb_medals_18.asp|archive-date=2019-01-20|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201902/rnoti-p261.pdf|title=Guionnet Awarded Pascal Medal|department=Mathematics People|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|date=February 2019|page=261|volume=66|issue=2}}</ref> She became a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of members|publisher=Academia Europaea|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/List_of_Members|access-date=2020-10-02}}</ref>

She has been a Knight of the [[Legion of Honour]] since 2012.

In 2022 she was elected as an international member to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS)<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NAS Election |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2022-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220503174757/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2022-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 3, 2022 |access-date=2022-05-22 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> and International Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (AAAS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=American Academy of Arts & Sciences Announces New Members Elected in 2022 |url=https://www.amacad.org/news/2022-member-announcement |access-date=2022-05-22 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |date=28 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
